facts.fact: The Smart Zambia Institute's general procurement notice for the World Bank-financed Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (US$6 million preparation advance) lists a consultancy to develop technical specifications for a mobile-based digital authentication and e-signatures solution, including PKI requirements.
facts.system: mobile-based digital authentication and e-signatures solution

ZMB.note: The notice names INRIS only in a study of digital ID elements; no civil register link is stated.
The skills component targets underserved citizens, not civil servants.
The notice funds capacity building to operationalize the Data Protection Commission but does not say the law names it or that it is appointed.
No data protection law is described.
Last mile connectivity is not stated to be rural or underserved areas, and no rural and urban use figures are given.

facts.fact: The Smart Zambia Institute's procurement notice for the World Bank-financed Digital Zambia Acceleration Project includes a component on enhancing basic digital literacy, targeting underserved citizens.

ZMB.note: No e-commerce or electronic transactions law is named.
ZamPay is a person-to-government payments platform with no government service named.

facts.fact: The Smart Zambia Institute's procurement notice says the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project will support upgrading ZamPay from person-to-government payments into an integrated government-to-people (G2P) platform.

ZMB.note: Only a study covering ICT sector policy is to be procured; no policy is stated.
No count or share of people holding a national ID is given.
No number at birth is mentioned.
The notice calls the planned ID enrolment system home-grown but says nothing on who operates or maintains a system in service.
No public register keyed on the ID number is named.

facts.fact: The Smart Zambia Institute's procurement notice says that with World Bank ID4D support the government has chosen to develop a home-grown digital ID enrollment system based on open standards, and a study will review INRIS and digital ID requirements.

ZMB.note: Only a project implementation unit within the Smart Zambia Institute is planned, which is a project unit.
No local government connection is described.
The World Bank advance is a grant to the government; matching investments for infrastructure are only a planned manual.
No signed or ratified regional text is named.
No rural electricity access figure is given.
No school internet figure or curriculum statement is given.
